title: Peanut allergy diagnoses in US kids under 3, before vs. after early-introduction guidelines

source.name: Reduction in Food Allergies Found After Guideline-Directed Early Peanut Exposure (Pediatrics, 2025)

notes: CHOP researchers analyzed electronic health records for more than 120,000 children (through early 2020) and found peanut-allergy diagnoses in kids under 3 fell from 0.79% to 0.45% -- a 43% relative decline -- after the 2015 LEAP findings drove new early-introduction guidelines (2017 NIAID addendum, broadened by the 2021 consensus guidance). Overall food-allergy diagnoses fell about 36% over the same shift. Published in Pediatrics, 2025.
